angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 199,596 km at 27.36 pc = 0.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 36.5561 +/- 0.0175 mas (same row, RUWE 1.20): 27.36 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.2869 +/- 0.0088 solar radii from Srivastava et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-4552 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...709A..73S/abstract): 199,596 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.2619 +/- 0.0063 solar masses from Srivastava et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-4552 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...709A..73S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3258 +/- 115 K from Srivastava et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4552 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...709A..73S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Srivastava et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4552 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...709A..73S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-4552.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.941, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4552 (pscomppars): spectral type M4.5 V, from Srivastava et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...709A..73S/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, UPM J1738-4738: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4552 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.07 dex, from Srivastava et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...709A..73S/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4552 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -2.07779, from Srivastava et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...709A..73S/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
